title: Bond Price and Yield to Maturity

statement.md: A bond pays a coupon $c = F \cdot (\text{coupon rate}) / m$ at the end of each of $m$ periods per year, for $N = m \cdot \text{years}$ periods, and returns the face value $F$ with the last coupon. With annual yield $y$ (compounded $m$ times a year) and $i = y / m$:

Answer two kinds of queries. `P F cpn m years y` asks for the price with $y$ given in percent. `Y F cpn m years price` asks for the yield in percent, found by bisection of the annual yield on $[0, 1]$ (0% to 100%); the price is strictly decreasing in $y$. Print every answer with exactly 4 decimals. Tests only use prices that lie between $P(1)$ and $P(0)$, and keep outputs away from a rounding tie.

inputFormat: First line: $q$. Then $q$ lines, each a query as above. `cpn` and `y` are percents, `years` is an integer, `m` is one of 1, 2, 4, 12.
outputFormat: One line per query with 4 decimals.
hints: Price is a plain sum of discounted cash flows. Loop over periods.
For the yield use 100 to 200 bisection steps: lo=0 gives the highest price, hi=1 the lowest.

editorial.md: Evaluate $P(y)$ in $O(N)$. Because $P$ is strictly decreasing in $y$, bisection on $[0,1]$ converges to the yield; 100 halvings give far more than the 4 decimals needed.
A bond priced at par has yield equal to the coupon rate. That is a useful self check.
